text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The Szczecin-based Gryfia shipyard has started construction of the first of three ferries contracted by the town of Swinoujscie.
The new vessels will carry 34 cars and up to 700 passengers each, Swinoujscie president Krzysztof Adranowski said.
- Poland's retail sales in January grew by 16 percent and wholesale sales by 53.3 percent compared with the same period last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.

- The ZPOW Agros-Lowicz vegetable and fruit processor's net profit in 1996 was 12.2 million zlotys on a turnover of 155.3 million zlotys against a net profit of seven million on a turnover of 115.3 million the year before, the company said.
- The Dutch-German Ahold/Allkauf group opened 34 wholesale and retail outlets in southern Poland in the last 18 months.
The Polish operation will start bringing profits in up to three years time, the chain's director for Europe and Latin America said.
NOWA EUROPA

- The National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, is not supposed to audit unlicensed banking institutions, the so-called parabanks, and it can only motion for action by the prosecutor, central bank official Andrzej Parafianowicz said.
- Engine maker Daewoo-FSO Motor -- a subsidiary of Daewoo- FSO -- and Daewoo Precision will start engine manufacturing at the Ciechanow-based plant in northern Poland.
The factory's annual output will eventually reach 500,000 engines, Daewoo-FSO Motor director Lech Barbarski said.
Daewoo Precision will invest $47 million in the engine project development.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- France's Renault automaker will not invest in production development in Poland as the firm's output potential in western Europe is already excessive, Renault Europe marketing director Philippe Gamba said.
- India's good tea harvest this year will cut tea prices on global markets, which will benefit Polish consumers as a result of cheaper imports, an Indian Embassy official Subash Vohra said.
ZYCIE
- The Lublin-based ZM Lubmeat meat processor will increase its share capital by 1.64 million zlotys through a new C-series share issue.
The company's sales reached 40 million zlotys in 1996.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
